name: users/migrations/0001_initial.py
summary: Initial database migration establishing the users application schema and user model tables
purpose: Creates the foundational database schema for the users domain, enabling identity management, authentication storage, and user-related data persistence within the Django backend
responsibilities: Create database tables for user-related models based on the app's current model definitions
Define columns for authentication, identification, and user profile data
Configure timezone-aware timestamp fields and default values
Establish referential integrity rules and deletion behaviors for user relationships
Register the migration state to ensure consistent schema versioning across environments
inputs: Django model definitions from the users app
Django settings configuration (e.g., AUTH_USER_MODEL, timezone settings)
outputs: Database schema artifacts (tables, columns, indexes, constraints)
Migration record entry in the django_migrations tracking table
Updated project state representing the initial users app schema
architecture_notes: This is a foundational schema migration within the identity and access management (IAM) bounded context. The presence of django.conf.settings and deletion imports suggests potential swappable user model dependencies or foreign key relationships to other domain entities. As an initial migration (0001), it serves as the immutable base of the users app's migration chain and should never be altered after deployment to production. It follows Django's declarative migration pattern, separating schema evolution from application logic.
improvements: Ensure a custom User model was designed before this migration runs to avoid conflicts with Django's default auth_user table
Consider splitting authentication fields (User) from profile attributes (Profile) to adhere to Single Responsibility Principle
Add explicit database indexes on high-cardinality lookup fields (e.g., email, username) if the default indexes are insufficient
Verify reversibility and test against the production database engine to prevent locking issues
Document any dependency on django.conf.settings to avoid environment-specific migration drift across teams
